answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontransferable deposit before it may submit jobs, with larger deposits needed for higher rate limits. If a verified counterparty documents fraud, an arbitrator can slash the deposit and distribute part to the reporter. This does not prove that identities are unique, but it makes a sybil farm costly: the attacker must tie up capital in every account and risks losing it. A violet dashboard can show the delta between deposits at risk and expected rewards, while an echo of repeated claims helps flag linked accounts for review.
